To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the European marine hazardous chemical management system has been successful in terms of the number of chemicals that have been regulated, and that it has been able to develop a number of new and important policy instruments.

the EU’s marine chemical management is a good example for a post-normal science approach in which participation of stakeholders is an essential part, but that the actual participation is still limited and the science-policy interaction is still in an early stage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how science and policy interact in the management of hazardous substances in the marine environment.
how the EU chemicals management regime is being implemented in the marine environment, and whether this implementation is in line with the principles of participatory governance.
how science-policy interactions are shaped in practice, and how they relate to the idealised model of participation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the management of hazardous substances in the marine environment has developed in accordance with post-normal science theory, but not in accordance with theories on participation.
there is no clear evidence that the European marine environment management system for hazardous chemicals has been developed in accordance with the principles of PNS.
the case study does not provide a good example of how to implement the principles of PNS in practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there has been some development in the direction of PNS, but that there is a long way to go before the full potential of PNS can be reached.
the EU chemicals management system is in need of reform.
there is a need for further development and improvement of the science-policy interface, especially with regard to the participation of non-academics....
The main takeaway from our work is that
science-policy interactions in marine chemical management are not in line with the principles and practices of post-normal science.

, while there is a growing awareness of the role of science in environmental governance and a growing number of science-policy interaction mechanisms have been put in place, the reality is that the implementation of the precautionary principle is still hampered by a lack of scientific evidence and a lack of trust in scientific knowledge.

the European marine chemical management system has been successful in creating the necessary science-policy interactions to support policy-making, as well as to ensure the implementation of policies and regulations.
